idiom_name: NVI/CRTP base handler with a template-method execute() (or a std::function guard chain)
implementation_notes: C++ has no dominant server framework, so the base action is hand-written: an abstract handler built with the non-virtual interface idiom (a non-virtual execute() that runs the security sequence and then calls a protected virtual business step), or a CRTP base that calls the derived handler without virtual dispatch. The enforcers are injected collaborators, and where handlers are dispatched by name or as callables, a std::vector<std::function<bool(const Request&)>> guard chain plus a std::function business step is the compositional equivalent. The inheritance form is still justified when all handlers share one lifecycle and the security sequence is fixed; it is the closest native expression of the pattern.
pitfalls: A public virtual security step invites subclasses to skip checks; keep execute() non-virtual, the steps private, and only the business step virtual.
Handlers used polymorphically need a virtual destructor, and passing them by value slices the derived state.
Registries populated during static initialization have an unspecified order across translation units; build the handler map explicitly at startup instead.
